 Judgment

MFA No.4744/2012 is preferred by the 2nd respondent-New India Assurance Company Limited and MFA CROB No.63/2016 is preferred by the petitioner- K.Baburaya Sheregar, against the judgment and award dated 26.11.2011 passed in MVC No.806/2005 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Member, Additional MACT, Kundapura.

2. By the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner holding that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence of both the 1st respondent and the rider of Bajaj M-80 and fixing contributory negligence on them in the ratio of 50:50 and awarding a sum of Rs.62,150/- as compensation (after deducting of 50%) and directing respondent Nos. 1 and 2 to deposit the same and dismissing the petition against respondent No.3- National Insurance Company Limited.
3. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
4. The brief facts are as below:

sentences.text: That on 14.3.2005 at about 08.30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in Bajaj M-80 bearing Reg.No.KA-20-J-417 and his son Srikanth was riding the same very slowly from Uppinakudru towards Kundapura, while proceeding on N.H.17 in front of Pravasi Hotel, Tallur, a Qualis bearing Reg No.KA-19-P-388 belonging to the respondent No.1 driven by himself came from Byndoor side in rash and negligent manner and dashed on the back side of the Motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding and did not stop after the accident.
Due to the said impact, petitioner and his son fell on the side of the road and sustained grievous injuries.

After the accident petitioner was immediately shifted to Chinmayi Hospital, Kundapura, wherein he was treated as inpatient from 14.03.2005 to 24.03.2005 and still he is under treatment as an outpatient.

It is claimed that the petitioner spent a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards medical expenses, a sum of Rs.2,000/- towards conveyance charges, a sum of Rs.3,000/- towards food and extra nourishment, a sum of Rs.2,000/- towards nursing and attendant charges.

5. It was the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and had well built physique, doing Business having monthly income of Rs.5,000/- and the accidental injuries resulted in mental anguish which greatly impaired general health of the petitioner and due to which, still he is unable to walk properly, as such sustained permanent disability.
On these grounds he prayed for compensation of Rs.2,34,000/- together with interest at 12% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
6. On service of notice by the Tribunal, 1st respondent remained exparte.

The 2nd and 3rd respondent appeared through their advocate and filed their separate written statements denying the petition averments regarding the age, occupation, income and expenses, rash and negligent driving of Qualis bearing Reg. No. KA-19-P- 388 by its driver.

The 2nd respondent further contended that driver of Qualis had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicles and that the accident solely occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of riding of Bajaj M-80 bearing Reg.
No. KA-20-J-417 by its rider.

Hence, the rider, owner and insurer of Bajaj M-80 bearing Reg. No.
KA-20-J-417 shall also be necessary party to the proceedings and hence, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

It is further contended that, in case compensation awarded the petitioner is not entitled for interest at more than 6% p.a. and also sought leave to contest the case U/Sec. 170 of M. V. Act if respondent No. 1 fails to contest and on these grounds prayed to dismiss the case with costs.
7. The respondent No. 3 contented that the accident was not due to the negligence of the M-80 motorcycle rider, denied the age, income and occupation of the injured.
It was admitted that as on the date of alleged accident the both vehicles were duly insured by respective insurers but the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues for its consideration.
Before the Tribunal, petitioner got examined himself as PW1, examined Dr. Dinesh Kumar Shetty as PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P47 in his evidence.
On behalf of respondents, one witness has been examined as RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R13.

10. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the 2nd respondent-New India Assurance Company Limited and the petitioner are before this Court in appeal and cross objection seeking appropriate reliefs.

11. The appellant Insurance Company contends that the Tribunal failed to note that the rider of the motor cycle is none other than the son of the petitioner and the rider, after filling the petrol from the bunk which is situated on the western side of national high way, in negligent manner he entered the highway without caring for the vehicles plying on the high way and dashed against the side of the - 10 - car.
It is contended that the Qualis vehicle which was plying from north to south, the motor cycle rider dashed the Qualis to the front right side of the car resulting in the accident.
It is contended that without appreciating these facts, the Tribunal erred in fastening liability on the Insurance Company at 50%.

It is also contended that the accident took place on the left side of (the eastern side) the road and therefore, the spot of the accident clearly establish that it was due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the M80 motor cycle.

Further it is contended that the police have filed the chargesheet against the rider of the motor cycle and at a belated stage, the rider of the motor cycle himself lodged a private complaint to the Magistrate and the same was referred to the police for investigation.

After investigation, a report was submitted in the said private complaint that the accident was due to the negligence of the rider himself and not due to the negligence of the driver of Qualis vehicle.

Therefore, it is contended that the Tribunal did not appreciate this aspect and it grossly erred in fastening the liability on the Insurer - 11 - K Baburaya Sheregar vs Sri Keshava Ameen on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157870876/

12. The petitioner who had sustained the injuries in the accident, has also filed a cross objection with certain delay.

Application which has been filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking to condone the delay states that the petitioner after receiving the notice through his Advocate came to know that the insurance company had filed the appeal before this court.
Due to the poverty and financial difficulties he could not approach any advocate in Mangalore and therefore, he was unable to file the appeal against the meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
It is contended that he was of ill health and he was a senior citizen and therefore, he was unable to file an appeal in time and therefore, the delay of 1107 days in filing the appeal be condoned.

Apart from the above contention, in the cross objection, the cross objector/petitioner has contended that the Tribunal has not appreciated the facts and circumstances of the case and that petitioner has sustained comminuted segmental fracture of both the bones of left leg, lacerated wound over left ankle, left knee, fracture of the lateral malleolus of left ankle and as such, he sustained the disability.
He is facing difficulty in doing his routine work and he is not in a position to do any work after the accident.

It is contended that the income of the petitioner was taken at Rs.2,500/- per month which is very low and the Tribunal ought to have taken the income at Rs.5,000/- per month as he was doing some petty business etc., prior to the accident.

He contends that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000 towards future loss of income which was not proper and the multiplier method was not adopted by the Tribunal and the disability assessed by the Doctor was also not appreciated by the Tribunal in proper way.
Therefore, it is contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and as - 13 - such, there is a need for reassessment of the compensation.
Apart from that, he also contends that the Tribunal did not properly appreciate the private complaint filed regarding the negligence.

It is contended that though the 'B' report was filed by the police, the Tribunal failed to appreciate that the chargesheet was filed on the basis of the complaint lodged by the driver of the Qualis at the first instance and as such, police had failed to appreciate that there was negligence only on the part of the Qualis driver.
Therefore, he has assailed the finding of the contributory negligence by the Tribunal.

22. After hearing the arguments by both the sides, the points that arise in the appeal and the cross objection for consideration are:
2007 ACJ 1928 - 19 - (I) Whether there was any contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the Qualis car and if so, to what extent?
(II) Whether the quantum of the compensation arrived at by the Tribunal is proper and correct?

(III) Whether the respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner,
who is the insurer of the motor cycle?
23. The fact that there was an accident involving the M80 motor cycle driven by the son of the petitioner is not in dispute.
So also the fact that the petitioner herein in the owner of the motor cycle and it had met with the accident is not in dispute.
The petitioner contends that the driver of Qualis car came from his back side and dashed against the M80 motor cycle of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that the said private complaint was filed on 8-4-2005.
Admittedly, the accident happened on 14-3-2005.

In the - 20 - private complaint which was filed by the son of the petitioner Srikanth, it was stated that on the date of the accident, the said Srikanth was riding the M80 motor cycle bearing No.KA.20.J-417 with the petitioner as the pillion rider.
While he was coming from Uppinakudru Towards Kundapura, the Qualis vehicle came from Byndoor side and dashed against the back side of the motor cycle.
As a result, petitioner sustained injuries and he was admitted to hospital.

It is worth to note that the private complaint which was filed by Srikanth was investigated by the investigating officer and 'B'
report has been filed stating that the negligence was on the part of the petitioner himself and there was no such negligence on the part of the driver of the Qualis car.

The petitioner, in order to establish that there was negligence on the part of the Qualis driver, relies upon the private complaint filed by his son which is produced at Ex.P1.
24.
In the said private complaint also, it was mentioned that the driver of the Qualis car came from - 21 - Kundapura side and dashed against the back side of the M80 motor cycle.
The 'B' report filed by the police in respect of the private complaint is produced at Ex.R4.

This document shows that the driver of the Qualis car, Keshava Ameen had lodged his complaint on the date of the accident itself,
wherein, he has stated that the M80 motor cycle came from the western side to the eastern side and while the Qualis was moving towards the south on the left lane of the road, the front portion of the M80 motor cycle hit to the front right side portion of the Qualis car and caused the accident.
Therefore, it is contended that the negligence was on the part of the rider of the motor cycle and he without taking care and seeing the vehicles coming from his left side i.e. Kundapura side, had entered the road negligently and thereby met with an accident.
25.
The complaint filed by Keshava Ameen is produced at Ex.R2 and the FIR at Ex.R1.

It is also pertinent to note that the spot panchanama produced at - 22 - Ex.R3 discloses that the road is about 25 feet wide and the accident happened at the center of the road and the mahazar which was conducted on 14-3-2005 clearly establish that it was not on the left side of the road.

Ex.R3 shows that the M80 motor cycle rider, who is the son of the petitioner came from Uppinakudru in order to go towards Kundapura he joined the road and without seeing the vehicle which was coming from his left side, he tried to enter the left lane of the high way and dashed the front right portion of the car.
The panchanama shows that the spot of the accident is in the center of the road.

It is relevant to note that IMV report is produced at Ex.R9 and it shows that the Qualis vehicle bearing No.KA.19.P-388 had sustained damages on the front right side wheel K Baburaya Sheregar vs Sri Keshava Ameen on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157870876/
9 mudguard and front right side indicator and bumper was damaged.

sentences.text: Whereas, the vehicle bearing No. KA.20.J.417, Bajaj M80 motor cycle sustained damages to the handle bar, gear lever, front left side footrest, front left side fiber shield damaged.

Thus, it is evident that the M80 motor cycle rider was about to enter the left lane of the high way - 23 - and in his effort to join the road, front portion of the motor cycle came into contact with the front right portion of the car and therefore, there are damages.
26.
The contention of the appellant herein is that, he was coming from the Byndoor side and the car came from Byndoor side and dashed at the back.
If at all, if there was a collision between the motor cycle and the car, the back side of the motor cycle should have sustained the damages.
There were no damages on the rear side of the motor cycle.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that there was negligence solely on behalf of the car driver cannot be accepted.

27. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company that the chargesheet has been filed against the rider of the motor cycle, i.e. the son of the petitioner and there was no such investigation report which indicates the negligence on the part of the driver of - 24 - Qualis car.
Therefore, he contends that the fastening of the liability on the Qualis driver and the appellant cannot be accepted.
28. The perusal of the documents produced in the form of Police report indicate that it was high way and the Qualis vehicle came from north to south.
The petitioner and the rider of the motor cycle entered the high way from the west towards east and they were also about to go towards south.
When he entered the road, obviously, the rider of the motor cycle did not see the Qualis vehicle which was coming from Byndoor side i.e. from the south to the north.
As a result, the driver of the Qualis could not control the vehicle and it appears that the front of the motor cycle brushed the front right corner of the car.
As a result, the handle bar of the motor cycle was damaged.
There was absolutely no damage to the rear side of the motor cycle.

This indicates that the driver of the Qualis car had also not taken sufficient precautions, did not - 25 - anticipate that the rider or pedestrian may come from right side where petrol bunk is situated.
29. The actionable negligence which is contemplated against the driver of the vehicles in any motor accident cases is that, whether any precaution taken by him would have saved the accident.
A driver should always be in the anticipation that the pedestrian or some obstacle may come from either side of the road and he is able to control the vehicle.

The circumstances which are brought out in the form of the evidence indicate that the rider of the motor cycle had entered the high way from the K Baburaya Sheregar vs Sri Keshava Ameen on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157870876/
10 western side and he was about to go towards the south.

entities.text: K Baburaya Sheregar vs Sri Keshava Ameen
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The driver of the Qualis also moving towards south and it is evident that the motor cycle rider was visible for him from quite a long distance.
If the Qualis driver was not in the moderate speed or controllable speed, definitely, the accident would have been averted.
The motor cycle had crossed half of the road from the petrol pump side and was on entering - 26 - the left lane while going towards south.

If the driver of the Qualis car could not control his vehicle and he did not anticipate that a pedestrian or motor cyclist may come across, it is evident that there was also negligence on the part of the Qualis car.
It is also not that the road had any curve and the driver of the Qualis had no view of the motorcycle from some distance.
Therefore it cannot be said that there was absolutely no actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Qualis.
30. It is evident that the investigation is done by the investigating agency, i.e. the police department from the angle of the culpable negligence.
It is evident that in the said accident, the son of the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle, entered the high way without seeing the oncoming Qualis car.
As a result, he dashed across the front right corner of the Qualis car and fell into the accident.
Obviously, while crossing the road or entering the high way, greater care and caution should have been - 27 - exercised by the rider of the motor cycle.
On that count, it appears that the investigation officer came to the conclusion that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
Under these circumstances, the finding given by the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the Qualis vehicle appears to be correct.
Moreover, the panchanama indicates that the accident was at the center of the road.

Though the learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that the accident had happened on the left side of the road, it is evident that the spot mahazar is clear enough is saying that the accident is at the center of the road.
31. These aspects have been considered by the Tribunal and therefore, I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.

Further, it is also relevant to note that the Tribunal has considered the fact that the rider of the motor cycle contributes negligence and also the Qualis driver has contributed the negligence but the greater - 28 - degree of the negligence is on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

Having considered the fact that the drivers of the heavier vehicles have to exercise more caution while driving the same, the Tribunal had come to the conclusion that the negligence on the part of the Qualis driver was 50%
and therefore, it held the contributory negligence at the ratio of 50:50.
Hence, no interference is needed in respect of the contributory negligence held by the Tribunal.

The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that there was no such negligence on the part of the Qualis driver cannot K Baburaya Sheregar vs Sri Keshava Ameen on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157870876/
11 be accepted.

sentences.text: to contend that it is a case of composite negligence.

I am afraid that the concept of (2015) 9 SCC 273 MFA No.7204/2014 & CON.MATTERS Disposed of on 25-1-2021.
- 29 - composite negligence cannot be applied to the case on hand.
The petitioner happens to be the owner of the one of the vehicle and respondent No.1 happens to be the owner of the other offending vehicle.
Therefore, for the petitioner, at no stretch of imagination it can be held that it is the case of composite negligence.

If at all, if there is any contributory negligence by the rider of the motor cycle,
the petitioner being the owner of the vehicle is vicariously liable for such negligence and therefore,
the principles laid down in Khenyei's decision would not be applicable to the case on hand.
